cards.note: No agent/session lifecycle listener: the plugin registers webServer routes, llm providers and its own cordis services only.
Plugin never boots or audits a config tree through @deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot; scripts only inspect packaged files.
No ctx.sessions use and no Session history reads (eventAt/snapshotEvents/ownEvents absent).
Plugin declares no SessionEventMap event and rewrites no message content, so no message projection is needed.
No HMR/config-reload wiring: no ctx.hmr.registerConfig call and no loader entry mutation.
The bundle patch mounts only the plugin's own rows; no profile or test composition mounts session-log-deepseek.
No code-runtime dependency, row or provider; the plugin registers no program-execution seam.
No SandboxProvider implementation and no ctx.sandbox.confine call site.
No ctx.shell implementor or consumer; the plugin owns no background shell command.
No ctx.subprocess provider; upstream HTTP calls use fetch, not the subprocess seam.
No workflow-engine provider row or configuration in the bundle patch.
No MCP client dependency, configuration or foreign-transport adaptation.
No MCP resource surface: the plugin neither mounts mcp-resources nor implements an MCP bridge.
No SSH/remote execution world use; all supplier calls are local HTTP.

Adapter now projects offloaded marks, computes each retained occurrence's exact request-version bytes and reports IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED instead of shrinking the request itself; 0.1.5 hosts fall back through a namespace guard.
Plugin never configures the llm-deepseek route or DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL; upstreams are third-party OpenAI-compatible suppliers.
No import from @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek and no custom model catalog with imagePixelBudget.
Usage accounting lives in the plugin's own store; it reads no tokenMeter state and no persisted context projection.
No AssistantProvenance/replay type imported or re-declared on either face.
Client half imports only Button/Switch from ui-primitives; no conversation node types or provenance views.
No InputTriggerSource registration, so no CommandClaim is built.
Plugin renders no composer tool-row permission control and reads no permissions projection.
No ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register / registerCloseHandler use in the client half.
ConnectionIndicator is neither imported nor rendered; the local primitives shim declares only Button and Switch.
Neither DiffBlock nor diffTotals is imported or used.
The client half is built and tested through vite bundles plus node --test; the removed ?fixture page was never used.
Patch only inserts the plugin's own rows; no workflow-worker-thread id or spawn config.
Offloaded occurrences are rendered as offloadedImageText placeholders before serialization, and the legacy nested tool-result path is guarded too, so marked images are never re-sent as bytes.
The plugin relies on no base tool rows, so the tool-ralph default does not touch it.
No mcp-resources row is added by the bundle patch or by a deployment overlay in this repo.
The patch names no code-runtime row and the plugin needs none of the new terminal/session-settings seats.
All five DSH peers and the two runtime packages still exist at 0.2.0-rc.1; no retired coordinate is referenced.
No headless automation or CLI output parsing in the repository.
No @deepseek-ai/dsh-package-manifest import; the manifest is a plain package.json.
No experimental package dependency and no mirrored release set.
Lockfile already resolves node-addon-require-builtin 0.1.9 with spec ^0.1.6; no stale 0.1.4 resolution to delete.
Documented as a web-profile plugin (bundle patch supports web only); Desktop installability is not a goal, so peer re-declaration is not required.
Negative evidence (session format, engine floor, launcher grammar unchanged); no source action.
Client half resolves no session list; the dock component receives sessionId as an injected slot prop.
Dock declares only the injected sessionId prop; neither useSessionPendingInteraction nor useSessionStatus is used.
Informational: the plugin ships dsh.bundle.patch, so it is fully manageable as a profile bundle through the Plugins page and dsh plugin; nothing to change.
Fleet/upgrade-window note about npm publish lag; no repository action.
No named *16 icon imports: the client draws inline SVGs and imports only Button and Switch from ui-primitives.
No workspaceFiles/readBytes use; the client talks to /router/api/* over fetch.

The plugin never used the legacy global settings store: keys/suppliers/usage persist in the profile-anchored data dir, and the exported Config is a deliberately empty volatile schema feeding the Models card mirror.
The plugin ships no agent presets and declares none in its bundle.
No raw session log parsing; all session-adjacent data is the plugin's own usage JSON.
No official DeepSeek provider config in this repository; supplier modules speak each vendor's own OpenAI-style API.
Optional packaging capability: the single small patch file is sufficient and the plugin has no no-reload config fields to declare.
Loader-level tolerance behaviour; the plugin has no composition action.

Capability already in use: every row ships locale/<lang>.json with meta.title/description plus its own package.json, which is exactly the 0.2.0 readPluginMeta contract; a package icon is optional and not needed.
The plugin stores no attachment payloads in session events; extensions get a JSON drawer via router.extStore.
Optional seats for a sidebar account launcher and a Models sign-in step; the plugin has neither surface, so they replace no workaround.
No spill-policy configuration anywhere in the plugin or its patch.
Informational vendored-dependency note; the lockfile is already on one coherent 0.2.0-rc.1 cohort.
Install-time registry selection is host/Plugin-Manager behaviour; no plugin action.
Informational workflow note (a client-bundle edit needs a host restart); no plugin source change.
DSH peer ranges widened to ^0.1.5-rc.2 || ^0.2.0-rc.1 so install and startup compatibility pass; verified with the harness's own evaluatePluginCompatibility.
No tool.call.toolview entry is registered by the client half.
No custom ConversationNodeDefinition is implemented.
The plugin never reads or writes the chat transcriptView setting.
Install runs are driven by the host Plugin Manager; no plugin source action.

The five @deepseek-ai/dsh-* peers, devDependencies and lockfile now carry the 0.2.0-rc.1-compatible corridor (^0.1.5-rc.2 || ^0.2.0-rc.1) as one coherent cohort; 0.1.5-rc.2 and 0.2.0-rc.1 both satisfy it.
Plugin does not read the Chat settings schema or assume a transcriptView default.
The patch inserts no rows relative to schedule/time-context/ui-schedule ids and assumes no schedule service.
Informational: the plugin's five row ids (dsh-router*) are unique and cannot collide with the new otel/product-analytics rows.
The plugin never forks sessions; the onCreated callback is not needed.
No local patch to @deepseek-ai/dsh-native-command in this repository.
